title: BERT
description: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model.
name: BERT
summary: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) is a transformer-based encoder model designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text. Unlike traditional sequence models that read text left-to-right or right-to-left sequentially, BERT reads the entire sequence of words at once, allowing it to learn the context of a word based on all of its surroundings.
use_when: Building NLP systems that require deep contextual understanding of words, such as sentiment analysis, named entity recognition, sentence similarity, and document embedding retrieval in RAG systems.
avoid_when: Performing generative text tasks (e.g. story generation, chat dialogues, translation) where an autoregressive decoder model like GPT/Llama is more appropriate.
pros: Bidirectional context learning enables superior understanding of sentence structure and word relationships compared to unidirectional architectures.
Highly customizable via fine-tuning on downstream tasks with minimal data and computation.
Robust and stable representations due to extensive pre-training on large-scale text corpora.
cons: High computational footprint for training from scratch compared to traditional recurrent networks.
Inferior performance on generation-based tasks due to the absence of an autoregressive decoder.
Strict context window limit (typically 512 tokens), making it less suitable for very long document processing without splitting.

key_hyperparams.name: learning_rate
key_hyperparams.note: Standard learning rate range during fine-tuning is between 2e-5 and 5e-5.

key_hyperparams.name: max_position_embeddings
key_hyperparams.note: Maximum sequence length that the model can process, governed by the positional embedding matrix size.

quick_start:
from transformers import BertTokenizer, BertModel
import torch

tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
model = BertModel.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')

inputs = tokenizer("Hello, BERT!", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)
last_hidden_states = outputs.last_hidden_state
decision_notes: Use BERT-base for local resource-constrained environments; scale up to RoBERTa or DeBERTa for competitive performance benchmarks on classification and extraction tasks.
research_background: Originally developed by Google AI Language in late 2018. Revolutionized natural language processing benchmarks by demonstrating state-of-the-art representations utilizing bidirectional masked transformers.
computational_requirements: Requires standard modern GPU (e.g. RTX 3080/4090 or T4/V100 in cloud) for fine-tuning. Multi-GPU clusters required only for training from scratch.
